settings.title: Lounge
settings.image_alt: Patterned neutral curtains beside a cream sofa and coordinated cushions in a sitting room
settings.caption: Palette, pattern and a sense of belonging.
settings.thinking: Echo the upholstery for calm; let texture or a single pattern carry the interest.
settings.consider: Competing focal points. A strong curtain pattern needs room beside artwork and furniture.
settings.blend_note: Warm ivory · let the furniture lead.
settings.coordinate_note: Soft taupe · carry the curtain pattern’s quieter colour through the room.
settings.lift_note: Pale ivory · a lighter tonal variation at the window.
settings.contrast_note: Deep taupe · a darker variation of the room’s neutral palette draws the eye.

settings.title: Bedroom
settings.image_alt: Soft grey curtains layered with sheers beside a bed and an upholstered chair
settings.caption: Softness in the room. Control at the window.
settings.lead: A softer way to end the day.
settings.thinking: Related tones keep the room quiet. Let texture add depth before stronger pattern.
settings.consider: High contrast raises visual energy. Choose blackout lining separately for light control.
settings.explore: Choose the mood at the window
settings.blend_note: Silver light · keep the window softly within the room’s palette.
settings.coordinate_note: Warm grey · echo the existing curtain and chair tones.
settings.lift_note: Soft chalk · a paler variation for a lighter visual presence.
settings.contrast_note: Warm wood · a deeper accent gives the curtain area more presence.

settings.title: Bay Windows
settings.image_alt: Warm full-length curtains following a bay window around a softly upholstered chair
settings.caption: A rhythm of light, fabric and architecture.
settings.lead: Let the shape do the talking.
settings.thinking: Tonal fabric lets the bay’s rhythm lead. A restrained surface keeps the folds readable.
settings.consider: Pattern repeated across several planes can feel busier. Plan stack-back before choosing visual weight.

settings.title: Patio & French Doors
settings.image_alt: Watercolour-patterned curtains framing glazed French doors in a light dining room
settings.caption: A considered connection to the outdoors.
settings.lead: A view when open. A presence when closed.
settings.thinking: A lighter tonal fabric keeps the view central. Colour can make closed curtains a feature.
settings.consider: A large fabric area amplifies colour and pattern. Leave clear space for access and stack-back.
settings.explore: Let light lead — or frame the view?
settings.blend_note: Soft stone · let the glazed area sit quietly within the room.
settings.coordinate_note: Watercolour blue · pick up a colour already running through the curtains.
settings.lift_note: Pale stone · imagine a lighter surface across the full span.
settings.contrast_note: Deep green · give the window a stronger frame, with more visual weight.

settings.title: Other Rooms & Windows
settings.image_alt: Green abstract curtains alongside a sculptural armchair and a quiet neutral wall
settings.caption: An individual room deserves an individual direction.
settings.thinking: Begin with the colours you want to keep, the daylight and how you use the space.
settings.consider: The room’s name doesn’t decide its style. Let your own reference lead.
